intro: Lesson 16: Medieval England in the 1300s and the wider world. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

keywords.def: the Middle Ages, about AD 1066 to 1500 in England
many lands ruled by one ruler

questions.q: Who was King of England in 1348?
Which ruler of Mali travelled to Makkah in 1324?
Core: Put eight events on the timeline sheet: 776 BC, 1066, 1324, 1325, 1327, 1348, 1381, 1485, and write the century for four of them.
questions.a: Correct order; e.g. 1324 and 1381 in the 14th century, 1066 in the 11th, 1485 in the 15th

questions.q: Extend: Write two sentences comparing England and Mali in the 1300s.
questions.a: England was mostly farming villages, while Mali had great trading cities and gold.

questions.q: Stretch: Why do historians say 'medieval' differently for different places?
questions.a: Each place had different events, so the 'middle ages' do not start and end at the same time
B) 14th. The 1300s are the 14th century: add one to the hundreds digits.

questions.q: Big question: England or Mali: who was richer?
questions.a: Mali's king, Mansa Musa, was famous for great wealth in gold
